about: Response classification (appendix A 1-6). Each case is one response as the tab returns it ({status, url, body} or {status, url, json} where json is serialized after an optional prefix; location for a redirect), how it was requested (mode: graphql for a query, page for a route document), and the outcome: ok, blocked (reason checkpoint | rate_limit), login, unavailable (exit 9), or failed (kind http | non_json | rejected_query | shape_changed). A checkpoint outranks a rate limit, which outranks a login.

cases.name: checkpoint-by-path
cases.fact: A final URL path of /challenge or /checkpoint (or below them) is a checkpoint: an indefinite block.

cases.name: checkpoint-by-path-on-query
cases.fact: The same path rule holds when a query lands there.

cases.name: lookalike-path-is-not-a-checkpoint
cases.fact: Only the path segment counts: /challenges is not /challenge.

cases.name: checkpoint-code-368
cases.fact: Error code 368 is a checkpoint.

cases.name: checkpoint-code-459-as-string
cases.fact: Code 459 is a checkpoint; a code may arrive as a numeric string.

cases.name: checkpoint-form-in-page
cases.fact: A document carrying a form that posts to /challenge or /checkpoint is a checkpoint.

cases.name: checkpoint-required-key-in-page
cases.fact: "checkpoint_required": true or "challenge_required": true is a checkpoint.

cases.name: checkpoint-url-key-in-page
cases.fact: A non-empty "checkpoint_url" is a checkpoint.

cases.name: checkpoint-url-key-in-query-body
cases.fact: The checkpoint keys are checkpoint signals whatever was requested: a query answered with an Instagram-style {message: checkpoint_required, checkpoint_url, status: fail} body is a checkpoint, not a changed shape.

cases.name: consent-required-message
cases.fact: An error message naming checkpoint, challenge or consent_required is a checkpoint.

cases.name: checkpoint-outranks-rate-limit
cases.fact: When a response carries both, the checkpoint wins: it is the stricter block.

cases.name: http-429
cases.fact: HTTP 429 is a rate limit: a 30-minute block.

cases.name: rate-limit-code-4
cases.fact: Codes 4, 17, 613 and 80004 are rate limits.

cases.name: rate-limit-code-17-string
cases.fact: A rate-limit code as a numeric string counts.

cases.name: rate-limit-code-613
cases.fact: Code 613 is a rate limit.

cases.name: rate-limit-code-80004
cases.fact: Code 80004 is a rate limit.

cases.name: rate-limit-message
cases.fact: A message saying rate limit, too many requests or try again later is a rate limit.

errors.message: Please wait a few minutes before you try again later.

cases.name: rate-limit-outranks-login
cases.fact: A rate limit is a block even when the same body mentions login.

cases.name: login-path
cases.fact: A final URL under /accounts/login or /login means login is required.

cases.name: login-required-message
cases.fact: A message naming login_required means login is required.

cases.name: csrf-message
cases.fact: A CSRF failure means the session is not usable: log in again.

cases.name: login-form-in-page
cases.fact: A document whose form posts to /accounts/login is a login page.

cases.name: page-404-is-unavailable
cases.fact: A route answered with HTTP 404 has nothing there: deleted or never existed (exit 9, do not retry).

cases.name: query-404-is-a-failure
cases.fact: Only a route's 404 says the target is gone; a query's 404 is a failed request.

cases.name: http-500
cases.fact: Any other status of 400 or more is a failed request.

cases.name: anti-json-prefix
cases.fact: A leading for (;;); is stripped before the JSON is read.

cases.name: data-with-nonfatal-errors
cases.fact: Usable data with a non-critical error list is still a result.

errors.message: A field could not be resolved

cases.name: no-data-critical-is-rejected-query
cases.fact: No data with a critical or execution-error message means Threads no longer runs this query as sent (its id or variables rotated).

cases.name: all-null-data-with-execution-error
cases.fact: data whose values are all null counts as no data.

cases.name: all-null-data-without-message
cases.fact: No usable data and no critical message is a changed response shape, not an empty result.

cases.name: app-shell-instead-of-data
cases.fact: An HTML app shell where JSON was expected is a changed shape.

cases.name: not-json
cases.fact: A body that is neither JSON nor an app shell is an incomplete response.

cases.name: rate-limit-json-on-a-document-read
cases.fact: A document read answered with a JSON error body is classified by its error fields too: the account signal does not depend on what was requested.

cases.name: page-ok
cases.fact: A 200 route document with no block or login signal is a document to read.

sessions.fact: A logged-in document carries csrf_token, NON_FACEBOOK_USER_ID (not "0") and username. When all three are missing and DTSGInitialData is present, the page is logged out. When only some are missing, the session cannot be established: report that, without claiming logout.

redirects.fact: A route read follows at most three redirects, only to https://www.threads.com. A post route that redirects to something that is not a post is unavailable (exit 9). A redirect without a location is a failure.
